compound.name: methyleugenol
compound.one_liner: Basil phenylpropanoid classed by EMA as a naturally occurring genotoxic carcinogen.

occurrences.source_citation: Muráriková A, Ťažký A, Neugebauerová J, et al. (2017) Characterization of essential oil composition in different basil species and pot cultures by a GC-MS method. Molecules 22(7):1221
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: METHYL-EUGENOL Plant 13-1400 ppm (Duke 1992). Paper states 'all the studied varieties, except from Lettuce Leaf, were methyl eugenol-rich' (includes 'Red Rubin' and 'Mammolo Genovese'); no individual values extracted. | Basis as recorded: ppm as listed by Duke (basis not stated per row; for 'Essent. Oil' parts it is ppm of the oil, 10000 ppm = 1 %) Basis (fresh/dry weight) not stated by the source; excluded from /compare until confirmed.

pharmacology.mechanism: Bioactivated by cytochrome P450 to 1'-hydroxy-methyleugenol and epoxide-diol metabolites that bind DNA; hepatic and other tumours in NTP rodent studies [5].

evidence.claim: Methyleugenol is a genotoxic carcinogen in rodents.
evidence.test_article_detail: methyleugenol (NTP rodent studies summarised by EMA)
evidence.outcome_summary: Hepatic tumours and other neoplasms; DNA-binding potency similar to safrole.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.detail: Present in most basil cultivars grown here, at levels that vary by cultivar and leaf age: six of seven cultivars studied were methyleugenol-rich, 'Red Rubin' and 'Mammolo Genovese' included [18].
safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: No numerical limit; EMA advises minimising exposure of young children and pregnant or breastfeeding women
safety_flags.source_citation: EMEA/HMPC public statement on methyleugenol, EMEA/HMPC/138363/2005

compound.teaching_note: The curation draft called methyleugenol 'minor in most cultivars'; the GC-MS study found the opposite, which is why the pack says 'most cultivars grown here' [18].
gaps: No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
Leaf-age dependence (ruling wording) not sourced in this pass.
Per-cultivar methyleugenol values not extracted from Muráriková 2017.
